chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abul Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to me from Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, who said: I heard Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him) say:

The people of Qum and the people of Aba are forgiven for visiting my grandfather Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) in Toos. And whoever visits him, and a drop of rain from the sky falls upon him while on his way, God will prohibit his body from the Fire.

key_terms.حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ جَسَدَهُ عَلَى النَّارِ: God prohibited his body from the Fire
key_terms.قَطْرَةٌ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: A drop of rain from the sky

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the shrine of Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) in Toos?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual merit of visiting the shrine of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) in Tus, specifically noting the forgiveness granted to residents of Qum and Aba. The unique detail that a single drop of rain during the journey sanctifies the body from Hellfire underscores the concept of divine mercy attached to the physical act of pilgrimage (ziarah) in Shia tradition.
